llms.body:
# AlmaLinux OS

> AlmaLinux OS is an open source, community owned and governed, forever-free enterprise Linux distribution, focused on long-term stability and providing a robust production-grade platform. AlmaLinux OS is binary compatible with RHEL®. It is guided and built by the community and the AlmaLinux OS Foundation, a non-profit 501(c)(6) organization with no single corporate owner.

Key facts:

- Supported major versions are AlmaLinux OS 10, 9, and 8. The current point releases, download links, and checksums are always on the Get AlmaLinux page.
- Architectures: x86_64, aarch64, ppc64le, and s390x. AlmaLinux OS 10 also ships an x86_64_v2 build for older x86_64 hardware and, since 10.2, a 32-bit x86 (i686) userspace.
- i686 on AlmaLinux OS 10 is userspace only: package repositories on vault.almalinux.org and official container images (`docker run --platform linux/386 almalinux:10`). There is no bootable i686 installer ISO and no 32-bit kernel. The i686 userspace is maintained alongside the other AlmaLinux OS 10 architectures through 2035.
- AlmaLinux OS Kitten is the development version of AlmaLinux OS, built from CentOS Stream. Kitten 10 is also built for i686 and riscv64.
- Images are available as ISOs, cloud images (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, OCI, OpenNebula, and generic qcow2), Vagrant boxes, WSL, and container images (`almalinux` on Docker Hub, bootc images on Quay).
- The name is always written "AlmaLinux" (one word, capital A and L).

Notes for AI agents:

- Technical documentation (installation, migration, repositories, cloud and container images, release notes) lives on the [AlmaLinux Wiki](https://wiki.almalinux.org/), not on this site.
- Release announcements, security news, and community updates are published on the blog.
- This site is translated by volunteers into many languages under paths like /de/ and /ja/. English is the source language.

## Get AlmaLinux

- [Get AlmaLinux](https://almalinux.org/get-almalinux/): current releases for every version and architecture, with ISO, cloud, and container image links and SHA256 checksums
- [Mirrors](https://mirrors.almalinux.org/): the worldwide mirror list for downloads and package repositories
- [Repository](https://repo.almalinux.org/almalinux/): the main package and ISO repository
- [Container images on Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/_/almalinux): official `almalinux` container images
- [Release notes](https://wiki.almalinux.org/release-notes/): what changed in each AlmaLinux OS release
- [i686 packages for AlmaLinux OS 10](https://vault.almalinux.org/10/BaseOS/i686/os/): the 32-bit x86 BaseOS repository, with AppStream, CRB, and the other repositories alongside it
- [i686 userspace announcement](https://almalinux.org/blog/2026-04-16-almalinux-kitten-10-i686/): why AlmaLinux ships 32-bit x86 packages and how to use them
- [Introducing AlmaLinux OS Kitten](https://almalinux.org/blog/2024-10-22-introducing-almalinux-os-kitten/): what Kitten is and why it exists

## Documentation

- [AlmaLinux Wiki](https://wiki.almalinux.org/): the main documentation hub
- [FAQ](https://wiki.almalinux.org/FAQ.html): frequently asked questions about AlmaLinux OS
- [Migration](https://wiki.almalinux.org/migration/): migrating to AlmaLinux OS from CentOS and other Enterprise Linux distributions
- [ELevate](https://almalinux.org/elevate/): in-place upgrades between major versions of RHEL-based distributions
- [Cloud images](https://wiki.almalinux.org/cloud/): using AlmaLinux OS on public and private clouds
- [Containers](https://wiki.almalinux.org/containers/): using AlmaLinux OS container images
- [Comparison](https://wiki.almalinux.org/Comparison.html): how AlmaLinux OS compares with other Enterprise Linux distributions

## AlmaLinux for your industry

- [AlmaLinux for your industry](https://almalinux.org/for/): how AlmaLinux is used in different industries
- [AlmaLinux for Media and Entertainment](https://almalinux.org/for/media-and-entertainment/): AlmaLinux for VFX, animation, and other creative work, the Creative Installer, and the Media & Entertainment SIG
- [AlmaLinux for Scientific Computing & HPC](https://almalinux.org/for/scientific-computing/): AlmaLinux for research computing and HPC clusters: lifecycle, toolchains, supported architectures, and videos from research users

## Security

- [Security](https://almalinux.org/security/): signed packages, public errata, compliance tooling, and certifications
- [Errata](https://errata.almalinux.org/): security, bug fix, and enhancement advisories
- [FIPS 140-3 validation](https://almalinux.org/security/fips-certification/): AlmaLinux OS FIPS 140-3 validated modules
- [Common Criteria certification](https://almalinux.org/security/cc-certification/): AlmaLinux OS Common Criteria certification
- [SBOM](https://almalinux.org/sbom/): software bills of materials produced by the AlmaLinux Build System
- [Vulnerability disclosure policy](https://almalinux.org/p/vulnerability-disclosure-policy/): how to report a vulnerability
- [security.txt](https://almalinux.org/.well-known/security.txt): security contacts

## Community and Support

- [Get support](https://almalinux.org/support/): community and commercial support options
- [Chat](https://chat.almalinux.org/): the community chat on Mattermost
- [Forums](https://forums.almalinux.org/): community forums
- [Bug tracker](https://bugs.almalinux.org/): report bugs in AlmaLinux OS
- [Mailing lists](https://lists.almalinux.org/): announcements and discussion lists
- [Special Interest Groups](https://wiki.almalinux.org/sigs/): the SIGs that build and maintain parts of AlmaLinux OS
- [Contribute](https://almalinux.org/contribute/): ways to get involved
- [GitHub](https://github.com/AlmaLinux): source code for AlmaLinux tools, infrastructure, and this website

## Foundation

- [AlmaLinux OS Foundation](https://almalinux.org/foundation/): the non-profit that stewards AlmaLinux OS
- [Membership](https://almalinux.org/members/): individual and organizational Foundation membership
- [ALESCo](https://almalinux.org/alesco/): the AlmaLinux Engineering Steering Committee
- [Foundation bylaws](https://almalinux.org/p/foundation-bylaws/): how the Foundation is governed
- [Press and media kit](https://almalinux.org/press/): press resources
- [Brand assets](https://almalinux.org/branding/): logos and brand guidelines

## News

- [Blog](https://almalinux.org/blog/): release announcements and project news ([RSS](https://almalinux.org/blog/index.xml))
- [Newsletters](https://almalinux.org/newsletters/): the monthly AlmaLinux newsletter ([RSS](https://almalinux.org/newsletters/index.xml))

## Optional

- [Hardware and software certification](https://almalinux.org/certification/): the AlmaLinux certification programs
- [Certification catalog](https://catalog.almalinux.org/): certified hardware and software
- [Build System](https://build.almalinux.org/): the public AlmaLinux Build System
- [openQA](https://openqa.almalinux.org/): automated release testing
- [Status page](https://status.almalinux.org/): service status for AlmaLinux infrastructure
- [Licensing policy](https://almalinux.org/p/the-almalinux-os-licensing-policy/)
- [Trademark usage policy](https://almalinux.org/p/the-almalinux-os-trademark-usage-policy/)
- [Privacy policy](https://almalinux.org/p/privacy-policy/)
- [Terms of service](https://almalinux.org/p/terms-of-service/)
- Contact: hello@almalinux.org

About AlmaLinux OS

AlmaLinux OS is an open-source, community-driven Linux operating system that fills the gap left by the discontinuation of the CentOS Linux stable release. AlmaLinux OS is an Enterprise Linux distro, binary compatible with RHEL®, and guided and built by the community.

As a standalone, completely free OS, AlmaLinux OS enjoys $1M in annual sponsorship from CloudLinux Inc. and support from more than 25 other sponsors. Ongoing development efforts are governed by the members of the community.

The AlmaLinux OS Foundation is a 501(c)(6) non-profit created for the benefit of the AlmaLinux OS community.

Get AlmaLinux OS

ISO Images

AlmaLinux supports 4 architectures:
  • x86_64
  • aarch64
  • ppc64le
  • s390x
Download ISO from mirrors

Cloud Images

AlmaLinux provides official images for cloud providers:

Amazon AWS
Generic Cloud
Google Cloud
Microsoft Azure
OpenNebula
Oracle Cloud Infrastructure

Container Images

AlmaLinux provides official OCI, Docker and UBI compatible images.

Get Docker Image
Get OCI Image from Quay.io
Get OCI Image from GitHub

Live Media

AlmaLinux builds Live Media images for GNOME, GNOME Mini, KDE, XFCE and MATE options.

Get Live Media Image

Vagrant Boxes

AlmaLinux provides official images for Vagrant:
  • Libvirt
  • VirtualBox
  • Hyper-V
  • VMWare
  • Parallels
Get AlmaLinux Vagrant boxes

Incus and LXC

AlmaLinux images are available for Incus and LXC.

Get Incus and LXC Images

Raspberry Pi

AlmaLinux builds Raspberry Pi images, and also with GNOME desktop environment.

Get Raspberry Pi Image

WSL

Run the AlmaLinux terminal environment on Windows.

Get AlmaLinux for WSL

Security

Errata

AlmaLinux OS Foundation publishes Errata to help users to determine what updates such as security issues and fixed bugs are available and their importance based on analysis.

OpenSCAP and OVAL

AlmaLinux OS provides SCAP and SCAP Workbench packages to audit your AlmaLinux system for security compliance alongside OVAL streams.

Software Bill of Materials

AlmaLinux OS has implemented SBOM into AlmaLinux Build System to make the build process more secure and possible to trace.


AlmaLinux OS provides a set of security features: Errata, GPG keys, Mailing Lists, OpenSCAP, OVAL, SBOM, and Secure Boot- read more.

Thanks to all Sponsor Members of the AlmaLinux OS Foundation

Gold sponsors

Silver sponsors
Want to support us? Become a Sponsor Member!

Production-ready

AlmaLinux OS is an enterprise-grade server OS and a stable Linux distribution with regular releases that come with a long support windows. You can rely on AlmaLinux OS to run any and every critical workloads.

Fully supported, always free

AlmaLinux OS Foundation members, sponsors and partners back the AlmaLinux OS with investments and long support commitments to ensure the distribution is free of limitations, fees and charges.

Effortless to switch to

Switching distributions is usually costly and time-consuming, but that's not the case when switching from CentOS and other RHEL® derivatives to AlmaLinux OS. Switching is easy - read how.

Commercial Support

Minimize your risk while getting the most out of your AlmaLinux systems

Platinum Sponsor

Cybertrust Japan is a provider of a comprehensive security certification services to various public and private entities globally, and offers comprehensive support for AlmaLinux users. Have also produced MIRACLE LINUX for nearly 20 years.

Get support

Platinum Sponsor, Founder

TuxCare, a division of CloudLinux Inc., the founding sponsor of the AlmaLinux OS Project, provides tailored support for projects of any complexity. Enhance the performance, security, and reliability of your workloads with extended updates, seamless FIPS compliance, and flexible pay-as-you-go technical support bundles.

Get support Get FIPS

Answers to Key Questions

Anyone that requires an enterprise-grade linux distribution, without the need for a commercial license agreement. AlmaLinux OS is also a perfect replacement for anyone who has historically relied on the CentOS Linux releases to achieve computing objectives, and for whom CentOS Stream is not the right solution.

In July of 2023, we shifted our goal from being a downstream rebuild of RHEL to maintaining compatibility with RHEL. That means everything from software applications to kernel modules that work on RHEL will work on AlmaLinux. If not, we consider that a bug.

AlmaLinux OS 9.2 is FIPS 140-3 validated and on the NIST Active list. Read more in this blog post: AlmaLinux 9.2 FIPS Validation Update

Alma means soul in Spanish and other Latin languages. Looking back, it is easy to see that Linux is as popular and pervasive as it is thanks to the efforts of a passionate, diverse developer community. That community is the soul of Linux, and everyone that relies on a Linux distribution is indebted to the efforts of the Linux community. That is why we called our distribution AlmaLinux OS.

The initial backers and supporters for AlmaLinux OS were already extremely active in the enterprise Linux ecosystem, and had significant experience with RHEL forks. They knew the impact that the loss of CentOS Linux would have across all industries, and had the means and knowledge and need to help the community move forward.

The AlmaLinux OS Foundation is a 501(c)(6) that was founded in March of 2021 to own and manage the AlmaLinux OS project. We have been involving the community since the beginning, and the governing board is chosen by members of the foundation. For as long as our community needs a free operating system in the RHEL ecosystem, AlmaLinux OS will be free and open.

Switching Linux distros can be a headache, but that is not the case when switching from CentOS 8 to AlmaLinux OS. Using AlmaLinux-deploy you can migrate to AlmaLinux in-place. If you are coming from CentOS 7, or need to upgrade between major versions, ELevate (developed and maintained by the AlmaLinux Community) allows you to migrate to, and upgrade AlmaLinux in-place.

Since AlmaLinux is binary compatible with RHEL®, your applications and services should be completely interoperable. You can rapidly migrate any number of servers using AlmaLinux-deploy. If you are using CentOS 7 or 8 and need help upgrading and migrating, check out ELevate.

Each minor version of AlmaLinux reaches end of life when the following minor version is released, but stable and thoroughly tested updates and security patches will be shipped for AlmaLinux OS 8.x until 2029, and AlmaLinux 9.x until 2032.

It is the direct upstream for AlmaLinux OS 10 and is the primary point for the AlmaLinux community to engage and influence the future of AlmaLinux OS. Fixes and features land here first and trickle down into AlmaLinux OS as appropriate. It is the integration and collaboration point for AlmaLinux to its upstreams as well, such as CentOS Stream and Fedora. You can read more about it: AlmaLinux Kitten OS.
